edits.old: It was Hanni. At night, when Günter was asleep and his hearing aid sat on the nightstand, she asked the blue light on the windowsill things she would never say aloud in the daytime. Marley didn't know it for certain; she only sensed it, from the way Hanni's gaze lingered a beat too long on the speaker. From the longing in it that had nothing to do with technology and everything to do with the solitude that can still sometimes stand in a kitchen even inside a thirty-two-year marriage.
